summary: 14-day analysis of Nightscout telemetry reveals excellent CGM coverage (98.7%) and an overall Time in Range of 86.0% (mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, CV 32.6%). However, clinical safety is compromised by excessive hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR), clustered heavily overnight (18.5% TBR at 01:00 local) and in the early evening (15.3% TBR at 19:00 local). The root cause is a combination of an aggressive overnight target (90 mg/dL), unannounced meals (0g carbs logged) driving delayed SMB stacking and dynamic ISF stiffening, and unsafe automation safety limits (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h) relative to a total daily dose of ~19.7 U.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is excellent at 98.7% over 14 days with no major gaps. Telemetry includes complete loop status logs, temp basals, and boluses, but zero carbohydrates were logged during the period.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM readings, largest gap 65.0 min, total_carbs_g = 0.0 across 655 insulin treatments.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged carb entries limits direct empirical assessment of carb ratios and absorption profiles.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall glycemic control is well-maintained (86.0% TIR), but Time Below Range (5.1%) exceeds the standard 4.0% safety threshold, driven by recurring nocturnal and evening hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7 mg/dL, CV 32.6%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1% with Level 2 extremes down to 41 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unable to distinguish sensor compression lows from true physiological hypos without fingerstick logs, though loop suspensions corroborate true drops.

analysis_steps.findings: The 90 mg/dL overnight target is overly aggressive, causing persistent low-glucose predictions and loop suspensions between 00:00 and 04:00 local, where TBR reaches 18.5%. A secondary hypo peak at 19:00 local (15.3% TBR) follows a basal step-up to 0.7 U/h.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hour 01 local TBR 18.5% (avg 90.6 mg/dL); Hour 19 local TBR 15.3% (avg 105.4 mg/dL); target segment set to 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True fasting basal assessment is confounded by unannounced meals and late-window IOB tails.

analysis_steps.findings: Static ISF (56 mg/dL/U) is heavily modified by Dynamic ISF during post-meal spikes, scaling ISF down to ~27-38 mg/dL/U. This aggressive stiffening causes over-correction and late-window hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: DIA set to 10.0h; post-meal peak at 16:00 local reaches 162.8 mg/dL (32.1% TAR) before crashing to 105.4 mg/dL at 19:00 local.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unlogged meal carbs prevent precise validation of static CR and ISF balance.

analysis_steps.findings: The system relies entirely on UAM logic and 3-minute SMB microboluses for prandial coverage. Because UAM reacts after glucose rises, insulin delivery is delayed, causing post-prandial spikes followed by severe stacking hypos.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of meal timing logs requires inferring meal onset from CGM rate of change.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits are dangerously high relative to user daily insulin requirements. Max IOB (25 U) represents 127% of total daily dose (~19.7 U), and Max Basal (12 U/h) is 15 times the maximum scheduled basal rate (0.8 U/h).
analysis_steps.evidence: max_iob_units=25.0, max_basal_u_per_hour=12.0, total 14-day insulin 275.95 U (~19.7 U/day).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens is disabled; sensitivity relies entirely on oref1 dynamic calculations.

analysis_steps.findings: Complete absence of pre-meal boluses forces loop automation to supply 100% of prandial insulin via UAM SMBs, creating a recurring pattern of afternoon spikes (14:00-16:00 TAR 32.1%) and evening crashes.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0 carb treatments logged; correction windows show drops of up to 178 mg/dL within 120 minutes following dynamic SMB delivery.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact meal macronutrient breakdown is unrecorded.

analysis_steps.findings: Default carb absorption settings (min 5m impact 8 mg/dL/5min, max absorption 7h) cause UAM to maintain decaying carb impact estimates long after meals, prolonging SMB delivery into periods of falling glucose.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No empirical carb entry data to test absorption decay curves against actual digestion rates.

analysis_steps.findings: A staged optimization plan is established: First, address immediate safety risks by raising the overnight glucose target to 100 mg/dL and tightening AAPS Max IOB / Max Basal safety limits. Second, transition to explicit meal carb logging with pre-boluses to resolve UAM-driven afternoon spikes and evening hypos.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of nocturnal hypo rates (18.5% TBR), high safety limits (25 U Max IOB), and 100% UAM reliance.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: User execution of carb logging is required to evaluate phase two profile tuning.

strengths: High Time in Range of 86.0% demonstrates strong baseline automated glucose control.
Excellent CGM data completeness (98.7% coverage) with minimal sensor data gaps.
Low glycemic variability with a Coefficient of Variation of 32.6% (below the 36% stability threshold).
Properly configured 10-hour DIA supporting realistic dynamic insulin decay modeling.
issues: Excessive overall hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR) exceeding safe clinical target bounds (<4.0%).
Severe nocturnal hypoglycemia clustering between 00:00 and 04:00 local time (up to 18.5% TBR at 01:00).
Unsafely loose safety limits: Max IOB (25 U) exceeds 100% of average Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U), and Max Basal (12 U/h) is 15x the highest basal segment.
100% reliance on Unannounced Meals (0g carbs logged) causing delayed SMB delivery, mid-afternoon hyperglycemia, and evening stacking hypos (15.3% TBR at 19:00 local).

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target to Reduce Nocturnal Hypoglycemia
recommendations.description: Increase the overnight target segment (23:00 to 08:00) from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL to establish a wider safety margin during sleep, directly mitigating the 18.5% TBR observed between 00:00 and 04:00 local time.

recommendations.title: Tighten AAPS Max IOB and Max Basal Safety Limits
recommendations.description: Reduce Max IOB from 25.0 U to a safer ceiling of 4.0 U (~20% of TDD) and Max Basal from 12.0 U/h to 3.0 U/h (~3.75x max basal) to protect against runaway SMB stacking and sensor anomalies.

recommendations.title: Announce Carbohydrates and Use Pre-Bolusing
recommendations.description: Begin logging meal carbs with a 10-15 minute pre-bolus to align insulin peak with absorption, eliminating reliance on delayed UAM SMBs that trigger post-prandial spikes and evening crashes.

suggested_change.action: Log carbs with 10-15 min pre-bolus and upfront bolus delivery.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the overnight target segment (00:00-08:00) from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight TBR reaches 18.5% at 01:00 local despite frequent closed-loop basal suspensions. Raising the target creates an immediate safety buffer during sleep without changing basal rates simultaneously.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight CGM readings for 3 to 5 nights to verify elimination of glucose values below 70 mg/dL.

Morning fasting glucose remains stable (TBR 1.3%-2.5%, avg ~99.5 mg/dL). Current rate supports waking requirements.
Midday glucose rise is driven by unannounced meals rather than basal deficiency. Retain rate until carb logging isolates prandial needs.
Late afternoon window is confounded by peak UAM SMB activity. Maintain current rate.
Glucose begins falling rapidly in this window due to stacked afternoon UAM SMBs. Keep rate unchanged until meal bolusing is established.
TBR peaks at 15.3% at 19:00 local. However, this is driven by stacked afternoon UAM SMBs rather than basal excess alone. Retain rate while addressing meal bolus timing.
No carbs logged in telemetry. Retain existing CR segment until meal entry is established.
Zero carb entries available to evaluate early morning carb sensitivity.
Morning excursions occur under UAM logic. Retain setting until meal carbs are declared.
Afternoon meal spikes (TAR 32.1% at 16:00) stem from UAM lag rather than proven CR inaccuracy.
Evening prandial responses are obscured by late UAM SMB tails.
Dynamic ISF active (70% factor) adjusts operational ISF dynamically between 27 and 56 mg/dL/U. Maintain static profile value until safety limits are calibrated.
Overnight TBR reaches 18.5% at 01:00 local. Raising target from 90 to 100 mg/dL increases safety buffer during sleep.
Daytime target of 100 mg/dL provides appropriate baseline alignment.
23:00 segment initiates the overnight low target window. Align with 00:00 target change to 100 mg/dL for overnight safety.
10-hour duration of insulin action matches recommended exponential decay modeling for oref1 dynamic sensitivity.
SMB and UAM functionality are required for the closed-loop setup, but meal announcements should relieve UAM workload.
Activation conditions are functional; safety improvements should be achieved via Max IOB/Max Basal bounds rather than disabling SMBs.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery timing settings are standard for oref1. Restrict overall insulin risk via global Max IOB.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current Max IOB (25 U) exceeds 100% of Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U) and Max Basal (12 U/h) is 15x max scheduled basal. Lowering to 4 U Max IOB and 3 U/h Max Basal restores critical safety guardrails.
Dynamic ISF effectively manages high excursions. Keep 70% adjustment factor while stabilizing prandial inputs.
Carb absorption settings are standard; retain until explicit carb logging is performed.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Announce all meals with carbohydrate amounts and apply a 10 to 15 minute pre-bolus with an upfront bolus (70-80%), allowing AAPS SMB/UAM logic to handle only residual post-prandial variances.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: 100% reliance on unannounced meals creates a 30-60 minute insulin delivery delay, resulting in 14:00-16:00 hyperglycemia (32.1% TAR) followed by severe evening stacking hypos (15.3% TBR at 19:00 local).
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Consistently log carbohydrates and meal timing for 3 to 5 days to verify reduction in post-meal spikes and elimination of late-window hypos.

exceptions.pattern: High-fat/protein or extended afternoon meals (14:00-17:00 local)
exceptions.suggestion: Split carb entry using e-carbs (e.g., 50% upfront bolus and 50% spread over 2-3 hours as e-carbs).
exceptions.rationale: Prevents initial over-bolusing while avoiding the delayed UAM SMB stacking that currently triggers evening hypoglycemia.

implementation_steps: Step 1: In the AAPS profile, adjust the overnight target segment (23:00 to 08:00) from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.
Step 2: Update AAPS safety settings: reduce Max IOB from 25.0 U to 4.0 U and Max Basal from 12.0 U/h to 3.0 U/h.
Step 3: Monitor glucose overnight for 3 to 5 days to evaluate nocturnal stability under the higher target.
Step 4: Begin announcing meal carbohydrates with a 10-15 minute pre-bolus for all primary meals.
Step 5: Re-evaluate 14-day telemetry after 1 week of consistent carb logging to assess true Carb Ratios and ISF accuracy.
education: Unannounced Meal (UAM) logic detects carbohydrates only after sensor glucose starts rising, introducing an inherent 30 to 60 minute insulin lag.
When UAM SMBs fire repeatedly during a glucose spike, insulin-on-board accumulates late in the digestion cycle, frequently causing hypoglycemia 2 to 4 hours post-meal.
Max IOB limits act as a critical safety brake in automated insulin delivery systems, preventing software or sensor errors from delivering dangerous insulin amounts.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change with their healthcare team.
Make profile changes one at a time, allowing at least 3 to 5 days of observation between modifications.
Always monitor blood glucose closely after modifying target segments or safety limits, and keep rapid-acting carbohydrates readily accessible.
